intro: Elementary teachers explain ideas simply, manage a full room and track each child's progress. The closest of the 25 careers below is adult basic education and ESL instruction, with a 95% skill match and a BLS May 2025 median of $61,540, about 4% less than the $63,970 elementary teachers earn.
why_it_works: A school day means teaching every subject, adapting lessons for different learners and keeping parents informed. O*NET rates instructing at 4.25 out of 5 for this job and social perceptiveness at 4. Adult education, training and social work roles build on the same skills. Many of the better-paid matches need a graduate degree. The gaps are budgets, analysis and complex problem solving.
tips: Corporate training is the fastest move: Training and Development Specialists earn $69,280, or 8% more.
Instructional Coordinators earn $77,440, which is 21% more, but usually need a master's degree.
Keep your license active while you test a new role through summer or evening work.

faq.q: What jobs can former elementary teachers do?
faq.a: The closest matches are adult basic education and ESL instructors (95%), Instructional Coordinators (80%) and postsecondary education teachers (80%), based on O*NET 31.0. Child, family and school social workers are 79% matched and earn $59,550, which is 7% less.

faq.q: Which careers for elementary teachers pay more?
faq.a: 17 of the 25 matches pay more than $63,970. Postsecondary area, ethnic and cultural studies teachers earn $85,020 (33% more), sociology teachers $84,290 (32% more) and psychology teachers $80,340 (26% more), according to BLS May 2025 data. All three need a graduate degree.

faq.q: Do elementary teachers need another degree?
faq.a: Often yes. Only 7 of the 25 matches need no more education than elementary teachers already have, and 18 usually need a graduate degree. A master's degree is common in close matches, held by 60% of workers in one of them.

faq.q: What skills should elementary teachers build?
faq.a: The skills that most often need work are managing financial resources, complex problem solving, operations analysis and managing materials. Coordination already rates 3.88 out of 5 for elementary teachers in O*NET, so business and analysis skills are the main step outside the classroom.
